newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks extend losses as profit-takers enter.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks extend losses as profit-takers enter.

text.p: Madrid stocks slumped even further in late trade on Thursday to close with losses in line with other markets. Profit-taking also took its toll, dealers said.
The general index fell 5.64 points, 0.90 percent, to 621.57 and the Ibex-35 lost 69.55 points, 0.97 percent, to 7,095.16.

Gas stocks took a beating after Spain's industry ministry said it was proposing a four percent industrial gas rate cut. Dealers said the shares in Gas Natural and Repsol would continue to be affected until the whole tariff structure was settled.
Gas Natural sank 3.33 percent to 33,000, while Repsol dropped 100 pesetas, 1.54 percent, to 6,480.

"We still don't know how the (gas) system is going to work...some bits and pieces are coming out but always a partial picture," one dealer said. "The performance of Gas Natural and Repsol will be affected during this period of confusion."
Dealers said the overall market was at comfortable levels, allowing some profit-taking for those who wanted it while prices consolidated ahead of a fresh upward march.
Volume was smaller than recent days with nearly 76 billion pesetas in shares traded. Telefonica lost 50 pesetas, 1.09 percent, to 4,520, and the big banks fell more than one percent.
